title: Combined HH/HV surface-change evidence
notes: Candidate patches show radar surface change, not independently verified burns, severity, biomass or recovery.
HH and HV changes are computed separately against each viewing group’s median linear-power baseline; raw opposite-view powers are never averaged.
The primary map combines the latest selected post-baseline observation per group. These dates are asynchronous; time frames show individual measured views, not a synchronized fused movie.
Robust normalization depends on the entire selected land window. Cropping or changing water exclusions changes the score and threshold result.
Native sample screening is applied before averaging. No per-track DEM/LOS terrain-shadow mask is implemented.
A supplied domain can exclude water; without a justified land domain, water and other unrelated changes can affect normalization.
Grid posting is not independent spatial resolving power: Gaussian full width at half maximum is 2.355 times smoothing sigma.
Input is a local native-grid area extract, not a complete original NASA product; only the saved rectangle can be analyzed.
GCOV source-sample mask is applied before averaging. It is not a terrain-shadow or water classifier.

report.headline: What these observations show
findings: 8 real GCOV observations from 2 viewing group(s) produced 7453.00 ha of candidate changed patches within 45228.56 ha of valid land.
Threshold z ≥ 2; patches ≥ 10 ha. Spatial normalization: median 1.9986 dB, scaled MAD 0.3636 dB.
This detects surface-scattering change. Independent fire evidence is required for burn attribution; no recovery or severity is measured.
report.comparison_basis: All declared baseline dates per view; latest valid view magnitudes averaged without filling missing pixels
next_checks: Inspect viewing-group coverage and the declared baseline dates.
Compare candidate patches with independent fire imagery and boundaries.
Check water exclusions, terrain effects and sensitivity to the selected land window.
report.validation: Paper-inspired change detection; case-study agreement does not establish accuracy in other regions.

properties.name: Terrestrial study window
properties.source: Sentinel-2 SCL water exclusions, 1 August and 12 September 2026; 30 m vector simplification. No optical burn-class thresholds used.

reading_guide.measurement: A combined HH/HV scattering-change score from separate pre-event baselines for each radar view, plus thresholded candidate patches.
reading_guide.colours: Higher z means more unusual unsigned radar change relative to this selected land window. The score is not a probability. Candidate 0 means the rule was not met, not confirmed unburned; the score can be negative.
reading_guide.checks: Check baseline dates and land exclusions, contributing-view count, smoothing and patch threshold. The latest contributing dates can differ by view. Assess terrain/shadow and compare with independent fire evidence.
reading_guide.cannot: Scattering change does not establish fire by itself, burn severity, burned vegetation type or ecological recovery. Case-study perimeter agreement does not establish accuracy for another fire.
reading_guide.validation: Source checksums verify input integrity. Replay checks verify reproducibility. Neither establishes independent environmental accuracy for this run.
